intro: These four second verbs say how far an action goes or which way it turns, not where it moves. 切る runs it to the very end, 合う makes it mutual, 直す and 返す do it again (to fix it, or back towards its source), and かける / かかる aim it at a target or leave it just begun. Find which of those ideas the sentence needs, then attach the second verb to the first verb's stem (the ます form without ます).

skills.rule: Stem + 切る means doing it all the way, until nothing is left; stem + 切れない means there is too much to get through.
skills.explain:
切る means 'cut off'. After a stem it means the action runs to its end with nothing left over: 使い切る (use up), 食べ切る (eat every bit), 読み切る (read to the last page). 売り切れる (sell out) is intransitive: the goods are the subject, 切符が売り切れた.

With a verb of state it means 'utterly': 疲れ切る (be worn out), 困り切る (be at a complete loss), 澄み切った空 (a perfectly clear sky). With a verb of saying it means 'without hedging': 言い切る (state flatly).

The potential 〜切れる is mostly heard in the negative: 食べ切れない (more than I can eat), 数え切れない (countless), 待ち切れない (can't wait).

The edge: 食べ終わる only says the eating stopped; 食べ切る says the plate is empty. 食べ過ぎる says you ate too much.
patterns: [verb stem] + 切る → do completely, use up
[verb stem] + 切れない → cannot get through it all
[state verb stem] + 切る → utterly (疲れ切る)
[thing] が 売り切れる → sell out

examples.jp: お金[かね]を全部[ぜんぶ]{使[つか]い切[き]って}しまいました。
examples.en: I have used up all my money.

examples.jp: この量[りょう]は一人[ひとり]では{食[た]べ切[き]れません}。
examples.en: I can't eat this much on my own.

examples.jp: 人気[にんき]のパンは朝[あさ]のうちに{売[う]り切[き]れた}。
examples.en: The popular bread sold out during the morning.

examples.jp: 一日中[いちにちじゅう]歩[ある]いて、{疲[つか]れ切[き]って}いた。
examples.en: After walking all day, I was completely exhausted.

examples.jp: 夜空[よぞら]には{数[かぞ]え切[き]れない}ほど星[ほし]があった。
examples.en: There were countless stars in the night sky.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]は「絶対[ぜったい]に勝[か]つ」と{言[い]い切[き]った}。
examples.en: He stated flatly, "I will definitely win."

contrast.note: 食べ終わる: the act of eating has ended, food may remain. 食べ切る: nothing is left. Goods selling out is 売り切れる.
食べ過ぎる: ate more than is good for you. 食べ切れない: could not finish it. Excess is 過ぎる, not 切る.

mistakes.bad: 夜空[よぞら]には{数[かぞ]え終[お]わらない}ほど星[ほし]があった。
mistakes.good: 夜空[よぞら]には{数[かぞ]え切[き]れない}ほど星[ほし]があった。
mistakes.note: Too many to get through is 切れない; 終わる only marks the end of an act.

mistakes.bad: 昨日[きのう]は{食[た]べ切[き]って}、お腹[なか]が痛[いた]い。
mistakes.good: 昨日[きのう]は{食[た]べ過[す]ぎて}、お腹[なか]が痛[いた]い。
mistakes.note: Eating too much is 過ぎる; 切る means finishing it, not overdoing it.

skills.tip: Ask 'is anything left?' Nothing left, or too much to finish: 切る / 切れない.

skills.rule: Stem + 合う means two or more people do the action to or with each other; 知り合う, 付き合う, 間に合う and 似合う are words to learn whole.
skills.explain:
合う means 'meet, fit together'. After a stem it makes the action mutual: 助け合う (help each other), 話し合う (talk it over, discuss), 励まし合う (encourage each other). The subject is plural (二人は, みんなで) or the partner is marked with と: 友達と話し合う.

Some 合う verbs are vocabulary in their own right. 知り合う: get to know someone (知り合い, an acquaintance). 付き合う: go out with someone, keep them company (買い物に付き合う) or have dealings with them. 似合う: suit (その服、似合うね). 間に合う: be in time, with に for the train or deadline (終電に間に合う); it has nothing to do with 'each other'.

The edge: a one-way action, one person doing it to another, cannot take 合う. 先生が私を助けた, not 助け合った. A useful check: if お互いに (each other) fits, 合う fits.
patterns: [A と B] が [verb stem] + 合う → do to each other
[person] と 話し合う / 知り合う / 付き合う
[train, deadline] に 間に合う → be in time

examples.jp: 困[こま]ったときは{助[たす]け合[あ]いましょう}。
examples.en: Let's help each other when things are hard.

examples.jp: 田中[たなか]さんとは大学[だいがく]で{知[し]り合[あ]いました}。
examples.en: I got to know Mr Tanaka at university.

examples.jp: 急[いそ]げば、まだ終電[しゅうでん]に{間[ま]に合[あ]います}。
examples.en: If we hurry, we'll still make the last train.

examples.jp: 家族[かぞく]で旅行[りょこう]の計画[けいかく]を{話[はな]し合[あ]った}。
examples.en: We discussed the travel plans as a family.

examples.jp: 二人[ふたり]は高校[こうこう]のときから{付[つ]き合[あ]って}いる。
examples.en: The two of them have been going out since high school.

examples.jp: その色[いろ]、とてもよく{似合[にあ]って}いますね。
examples.en: That colour really suits you.

contrast.note: 話しかける: one person starts talking to another. 話し合う: both sides talk it through.
話し込む: talk on and on, absorbed in conversation. 話し合う: discuss in order to settle something.

mistakes.bad: 先生[せんせい]が私[わたし]を{助[たす]け合[あ]いました}。
mistakes.good: 先生[せんせい]が私[わたし]を{助[たす]けてくれました}。
mistakes.note: One-way help with を takes no 合う.

mistakes.bad: 走[はし]ったので、電車[でんしゃ]を{間[ま]に合[あ]った}。
mistakes.good: 走[はし]ったので、電車[でんしゃ]に{間[ま]に合[あ]った}。
mistakes.note: What you are in time for takes に.

mistakes.bad: 彼[かれ]とは去年[きょねん]、仕事[しごと]で{付[つ]き合[あ]いました}。
mistakes.good: 彼[かれ]とは去年[きょねん]、仕事[しごと]で{知[し]り合[あ]いました}。
mistakes.note: Getting acquainted is 知り合う; 付き合う is dating, keeping company or ongoing dealings, not first meeting.

skills.tip: Can you add お互いに? Then 合う. If not, it must be one of the fixed words: 間に合う, 似合う, 付き合う.

skills.rule: Stem + 直す means doing it again to get it right; stem + 返す means doing it back: in reply, back to its owner, or over again from the start.
skills.explain:
直す means 'fix'. After a stem it means redoing an action because the first attempt was wrong or not good enough: 書き直す (rewrite), やり直す (start over), 考え直す (reconsider), 見直す (check again), 読み直す (reread to check). There is always a sense of correcting.

返す means 'return, send back'. After a stem it turns the action back: towards the person who started it (言い返す, answer back; 聞き返す, ask in return), back to its owner (取り返す, win back what was taken), or back to the beginning (繰り返す, repeat; 読み返す, read through again).

The difference: 直す improves, 返す reverses or repeats. 繰り返す is the everyday word for 'repeat' (同じ間違いを繰り返す); there is no 繰り直す. やり返す means 'get even', never 'redo'.
patterns: [verb stem] + 直す → redo it properly
[verb stem] + 返す → do it back: in reply, to the owner, from the start

examples.jp: 間違[まちが]えたので、名前[なまえ]を{書[か]き直[なお]しました}。
examples.en: I made a mistake, so I rewrote my name.

examples.jp: もう一度[いちど]最初[さいしょ]から{やり直[なお]そう}。
examples.en: Let's start over from the beginning.

examples.jp: 同[おな]じ失敗[しっぱい]を{繰[く]り返[かえ]さない}ように気[き]をつけます。
examples.en: I'll take care not to repeat the same mistake.

examples.jp: 弟[おとうと]は叱[しか]られて、母[はは]に{言[い]い返[かえ]した}。
examples.en: When he was told off, my younger brother answered our mother back.

examples.jp: 留学[りゅうがく]のことは、もう少[すこ]し{考[かんが]え直[なお]して}みます。
examples.en: I'll reconsider studying abroad a little more.

examples.jp: 盗[ぬす]まれた自転車[じてんしゃ]を{取[と]り返[かえ]した}。
examples.en: I got my stolen bicycle back.

contrast.note: やり直す: redo it properly. やり返す: retaliate. 書き直す: rewrite to correct. 読み返す: read through again.
もう一度言ってください simply repeats. 言い直す corrects or rephrases what was said.

mistakes.bad: 失敗[しっぱい]したので、最初[さいしょ]から{やり返[かえ]した}。
mistakes.good: 失敗[しっぱい]したので、最初[さいしょ]から{やり直[なお]した}。
mistakes.note: Redoing after a failure is やり直す; やり返す means hitting back.

mistakes.bad: 何度[なんど]も{繰[く]り直[なお]して}練習[れんしゅう]した。
mistakes.good: 何度[なんど]も{繰[く]り返[かえ]して}練習[れんしゅう]した。

skills.tip: Was the first try wrong? 直す. Does it go back to a person, an owner or the start? 返す.

skills.rule: Stem + かける aims an action at someone, or leaves it begun but unfinished; stem + かかる means passing by (通りかかる) or setting to work (取りかかる).
skills.explain:
かける adds two meanings to a stem. First, aiming the action at a person, who takes に: 話しかける (speak to, start a conversation with), 呼びかける (call out to, appeal to), 笑いかける (smile at). 隣の人に話しかける.

Second, 'begun but not finished' or 'about to': 言いかけてやめた (started to say something, then stopped), 忘れかけていた (had almost forgotten). The noun form 〜かけ is common: 読みかけの本 (a half-read book), 食べかけのパン.

出かける is simply 'go out', a word to learn whole.

かかる is the intransitive partner. 通りかかる: happen to pass by, with を for the place (店の前を通りかかる). 取りかかる: get down to a task, with に (宿題に取りかかる).

The edge with 出す: 泣き出す is a sudden start that carries on; 言いかける is a start that stops short.
patterns: [person] に [verb stem] + かける → do towards someone
[verb stem] + かけて やめる / かけの [noun] → begun, not finished
[place] を 通りかかる → happen to pass
[task] に 取りかかる → get down to

examples.jp: 明日[あした]は朝[あさ]から{出[で]かけます}。
examples.en: I'm going out first thing tomorrow.

examples.jp: 駅[えき]で知[し]らない人[ひと]に{話[はな]しかけられた}。
examples.en: A stranger spoke to me at the station.

examples.jp: 彼女[かのじょ]は何[なに]か{言[い]いかけて}、黙[だま]ってしまった。
examples.en: She started to say something, then fell silent.

examples.jp: 店[みせ]の前[まえ]を{通[とお]りかかった}とき、友達[ともだち]に会[あ]った。
examples.en: As I happened to pass the shop, I ran into a friend.

examples.jp: 昼[ひる]ご飯[はん]の後[あと]、すぐ仕事[しごと]に{取[と]りかかった}。
examples.en: Right after lunch I got down to work.

examples.jp: 机[つくえ]の上[うえ]に{読[よ]みかけ}の本[ほん]がある。
examples.en: There is a half-read book on the desk.

contrast.note: 泣き出す, 降り出す: a sudden start that goes on. 言いかける: a start that stops, or almost happens.
話しかける: one person addresses another. 話し合う: both discuss together.

mistakes.bad: 隣[となり]の人[ひと]を{話[はな]しかけた}。
mistakes.good: 隣[となり]の人[ひと]に{話[はな]しかけた}。
mistakes.note: The person you speak to takes に.

mistakes.bad: 宿題[しゅくだい]を{取[と]りかかった}。
mistakes.good: 宿題[しゅくだい]に{取[と]りかかった}。
mistakes.note: 取りかかる is intransitive: the task takes に.

mistakes.bad: 赤[あか]ちゃんが急[きゅう]に{泣[な]きかけて}、一時間[いちじかん]も泣[な]き続[つづ]けた。
mistakes.good: 赤[あか]ちゃんが急[きゅう]に{泣[な]き出[だ]して}、一時間[いちじかん]も泣[な]き続[つづ]けた。
mistakes.note: A sudden start that carries on is 出す; かける stops short.

skills.tip: Aimed at someone with に, or stopped halfway: かける. Passing by, or getting down to a task: かかる.
